Title: ELSA Journal
Description: A tool for embedding ethical, legal, and societal aspects in data science projects
Introduction:
This document is a record of the ethical, legal, and societal considerations that were reflected on during the course of this data science project. Data science projects, whether they involve building predictive models, analysing large datasets, or automating decisions, can have significant consequences for individuals, communities, and organisations. It is therefore important that the teams working on them regularly pause to ask difficult questions: about who might be affected, how data is being used, what risks might arise, and whether the approach taken is fair, transparent, and legally sound.

This document captures those reflections. It was produced using the ELSA Journal, a structured tool that guides project teams through a set of questions at each stage of their work, from initial problem definition through to data collection, modelling, and deployment. As well as prompting reflection, the ELSA Journal recommends relevant methods, tools, and frameworks that teams can draw on to support responsible ways of working (such as privacy impact assessments, fairness checklists, stakeholder mapping templates, and data documentation standards). Where the team consulted any of these resources, this is also recorded.

This record can be used to support ethics reviews, inform stakeholder conversations, meet reporting requirements, or simply help anyone involved in or overseeing the project understand the reasoning behind the choices that were made.
